name: versus-localqwen
description: IACDM orchestrator for local models served by Ollama in VS Code Agent Mode. Adds a context-budget guard for architectures without KV cache shifting, where overflow kills generation silently.
author: Jasmine Moreira

commands.title: Versus LocalQwen: Align Model Context Window
Versus LocalQwen: Clamp Ollama Token Estimator

versus-localqwen.ollamaUrl.description: Base URL of the Ollama server. Must match the URL configured in the Ollama extension. When VS Code runs on Windows and Ollama in WSL, point this at the VM IP or use a WSL remote window.

versus-localqwen.model.description: Model tag to monitor (e.g. qwen3.6:27b). When empty, the first loaded model reported by /api/ps is used, falling back to the first entry in /api/tags.

versus-localqwen.generationReserve.description: Tokens reserved for generation. A round is refused when the input leaves less than this margin. Matches the Ollama extension's defaultMaxOutputTokens.

versus-localqwen.statusBar.description: Show context-window health in the status bar.

versus-localqwen.usableBudgetFloor.markdownDescription: When the usable input budget falls below this, Versus offers to reset the Ollama provider's token estimate. Below `1` it is read as a fraction of the budget the host registered for the model; at `100` or above, as an absolute token count. The estimate drifts downward over a session, so this is the point at which the lost window is worth an interruption. Set to `0` to never prompt — the status bar still reports the live figure.

versus-localqwen.autoPatchOllamaEstimato.markdownDescription: Reapply the clamp on the Ollama provider's token estimator when an update removes it. The provider does not tokenize; it recalibrates a chars-per-token ratio against text that excludes tool calls and results, so in an agent session the ratio slides down and the usable window shrinks with it. The clamp stops the slide without blocking upward calibration. It edits a file belonging to the Ollama extension and keeps a `.versus-backup` beside it — set this to `false` to be asked instead, or to leave the provider untouched.

scripts.build: npm run compile && npm run compile:mcp && npm run bundle
